sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 593 was established by Ordinance No. 24476, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 13, 2000. Ordinance No. 24476 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 24476 was amended by Ordinance No. 24710, passed by the Dallas City Council on September 12, 2001. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 24476; 24710; 25163)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 593 is established on property located southeast of the intersection of Cockrell Hill Road and Interstate 30. The size of PD 593 is approximately 78.89 acres. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 24710; 25163)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) INDUSTRIAL (INSIDE) FOR LIGHT MANUFACTURING USE means a light industrial use where all processing, fabricating, assembly, or disassembly of items takes place within an enclosed building. Typical items for processing, fabricating, assembly, or disassembly under this use include but are not limited to apparel, food, drapes, clothing, accessories, bedspreads, furniture, decorations, artificial plants, jewelry, instruments, computers and electronic devices, and injection molding.

(2) ACCESSORY INSIDE RETAIL SALES means the inside retail sale of material or products manufactured, processed, or stored as a part of a main use allowed on a lot.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plans (Exhibits 593A and 593B). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the development plans, the provisions of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 24710; 25163)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The uses permitted in this district are all uses permitted in the IR Industrial Research District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the IR Industrial Research District, as set out in the Dallas Development Code, as amended. For example, a use permitted in the IR District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this planned development district only by SUP; a use subject to development

impact review (DIR) in the IR District is subject to DIR in this planned development district. Retail sales are prohibited, other than accessory inside retail sales. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted on the Property:

-- Accessory community center (private). -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. -- Home occupation. -- Private stable.

(c) Accessory inside retail sales are permitted by right. The area restrictions in Section 51A- 4.217(a)(3) do not apply to this use. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(b) Side and rear yard. No minimum side or rear yard.

(c) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio for all uses combined is 2.0 and 0.75 for office uses.

(d) Height.

(1) Residential proximity slope. If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope. Exception: Except for chimneys, structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through the slope to a height of 12 feet above the slope or 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(2) Maximum height. Unless further restricted under Subsection (d)(1), maximum structure height is 200 feet.

(e) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(g) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is 15. Parking garages are exempt from this requirement, but must comply with the height regulations of Subsection (d)(2). (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Required off-street parking.

(1) Office use: One space per 333 square feet of floor area.

(2) Commercial and business service use: Based on the individual use per Section 51A-4.202.

(3) Industrial (inside) for light manufacturing, freight terminal, and warehouse use: One space per 2,000 square feet of floor area.

(4) Office showroom/warehouse use: One space per 333 square feet of office space and one space per 2,000 square feet of showroom/warehouse floor area.

(b) Required off-street loading:

SQUARE FEET OF TOTAL REQUIRED FLOOR AREA IN STRUCTURE SPACES OR BERTHS

0 to 50,000 1 50,001 to 100,000 2 Each additional 100,000 1 additional or fraction thereof (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.109. SIGNS.

Unless otherwise provided by this article, the definitions, provisions, and regulations of Article VII, “Sign Regulations,” for business zoning districts apply to this district. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.110. SIDEWALKS.

No sidewalks are required. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Landscape Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.111. LANDSCAPE REQUIREMENTS.

Unless otherwise noted below, Article X applies.

(1) Soil requirements. Planting areas in general must have the following soil depths and dimensions:

(A) For each large shrub or small tree installation, a minimum of 24 inches of soil depth and nine square feet of surface area (total of 18 cubic feet).

(B) For each large tree installation, a minimum of 36 inches of soil depth and 16 square feet of surface area (total of 48 cubic feet).

(2) Irrigation requirement. All plant material used as required screening must be irrigated by an automatic irrigation system, installed to comply with industry standards. Other plant materials used to comply with these landscape requirements must be located within 100 feet of a

verifiable water supply unless naturalized vegetation is used. Proposed watering methods (irrigation or otherwise) must be:

(A) indicated on the landscape plan, if any; and

(B) adequate to maintain the plant materials in a healthy, growing condition.

(3) General maintenance. Required plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. The property owner is responsible for regular weeding, mowing of grass, irrigating, fertilizer, pruning, and other maintenance of all plantings as needed, unless an area is designated as “naturalized.” Any plant that dies must be replaced with another living plant that complies with these landscape requirements, and with the approved landscape plan, if any, within 90 days after notification by the city.

(4) Landscape plan review. The building official shall review each landscape plan submitted to determine whether it complies with these landscape requirements. All landscape plans must comply with the mandatory provisions in these landscape requirements. In addition, all landscape plans must comply with at least two “design standards” as described in these landscape requirements. The same landscape features and elements may be strategically placed so as to comply with more than one provision. (For example, the same large trees might be located so as to be classified as “street trees” and “parking lot trees.”)

(5) Mandatory provisions.

(A) Street buffer strip. A landscape buffer strip must be provided along the entire length of the portion of the street frontage of a lot, exclusive of driveways and accessways at points of ingress and egress to and from the lot. The width of the buffer strip must comply with the development plan.

(B) Site trees. One tree having a caliper of at least two inches must be provided for each 6,000 square feet of lot area, or fraction thereof, with a minimum of four trees being provided.

(C) Street trees. Street trees must be provided per Article X.

(D) Minimum sizes. Plant materials used to satisfy these landscape requirements must comply with the following minimum size requirements at the time of installation:

(i) Large trees must have a minimum caliper of two inches, or a minimum height of six feet, depending on the standard measuring technique for the species.

(ii) Small trees must have a minimum height of six feet.

(iii) Large evergreen shrubs must have a minimum height of three feet. For purposes of this subparagraph, “height” is measured from the top of the root ball, or, if the plant is in a container, from the soil level in the container.

(E) Buffer plant materials. Perimeter buffer strips are not required in areas designated as naturalized areas, or in areas that have a slope of 2:1 or greater. A Property owner may provide a landscape buffer strip or one of the following groups of plant materials at a minimum average density of one group for each 50 linear feet of the buffer strip:

(i) One large canopy tree and one large non-canopy tree.

(ii) One large canopy tree and three small trees.

(iii) One large canopy tree and three large evergreen shrubs.

(iv) One large canopy tree, two small trees, and one large evergreen shrub.

(v) One large canopy tree, one small tree, and two large evergreen shrubs.

(vi) Two large non-canopy trees.

(6) Design standards. Property owners must comply with at least two of the following design standards:

(A) Enhanced street buffer. A Property owner may enhance the street landscape strip to a minimum average width equal to or greater than 15 feet.

(B) Perimeter buffer. A Property owner may provide a landscape buffer strip along at least 50 percent of the remaining perimeter of a lot minus that portion included as a mandatory street buffer. The landscape buffer must have a minimum width of 10 feet.

(C) Enhanced vehicular pavement. A Property owner may provide enhanced pavement. This pavement must be at least 10 percent of all outdoor vehicular pavement on the lot.

(D) Permeable vehicular pavement. A Property owner may provide permeable enhanced pavement. This pavement must be at least 10 percent of all outdoor vehicular pavement on the lot.

(E) Pedestrian facilities. A Property owner may provide publicly accessible special pedestrian facilities and features such as plazas, covered walkways, fountains, lakes, ponds, seating areas, and outdoor recreation facilities. These facilities must occupy at least five percent of the lot area.

(F) Foundation planting strip. A Property owner may plant large shrubs along the foundation of the main building. The planting area for the shrubs must be a minimum of three feet in width and extend at least 25 percent of the portion of the foundation that faces a street. The shrubs must be spaced no more than six feet apart measured from trunk to trunk.

(G) Understory preservation. A Property owner may preserve existing healthy understory. The preserved understory must occupy at least five percent of the lot area.

(7) Tree preservation. Trees must be preserved per Article X.

(8) Private license granted. The city council hereby grants a private license to all of the owners of the Property for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the provisions of this article. A Property owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a landscape permit in accordance with the Dallas Building Code. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period; however, the city council retains the right to terminate this license whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or whenever the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163; 26102)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-593.113. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24476; 25163; 26102)
